featured.title: USCIS Says Your Green Card Application Is Now 'Extraordinary Relief.' That Word Does the Heavy Lifting
featured.excerpt: A policy memo reclassifies adjustment of status from a routine pathway to a discretionary favour, potentially forcing hundreds of thousands of applicants — many of them Indian — to leave the country and apply from abroad.
featured.image_caption: A USCIS Application Support Center in Jamaica, Queens, New York
featured.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders have relied on adjustment of status for decades to avoid the consular processing gauntlet — this memo threatens that pathway at the worst possible time, with consulate backlogs in India stretching into 2027.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Told a Packed Melbourne Arena He'd Made a 'Hat-Trick.' Outside, Anti-Indian Protesters Were Waiting.
news.excerpt: The Prime Minister's third Australian visit drew thousands of cheering diaspora members — and a far-right fringe demanding Indians leave. AustralianSuper committed $347 million to India's infrastructure fund the same day.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at a bilateral summit
news.nri_angle: One million Indians in Australia face rising anti-Indian sentiment even as Modi's visit strengthens trade and diplomatic ties between the two countries.

news.title: India's Refiners Were Eyeing Iranian Crude Again. Then Washington Killed the Waiver.
news.excerpt: Indian state-owned oil companies had been positioning for a return to Iranian oil purchases. The US revocation of sanctions waivers — and the collapse of the ceasefire — has scrambled their calculations.
news.image_caption: A crude oil tanker unloading at a port facility
news.nri_angle: India's 1.3 million Gulf workers face renewed instability as the US-Iran ceasefire collapses, while rising oil prices threaten inflation and the rupee for NRIs sending remittances home.

news.title: The White House Just Launched Its First Major H-1B Fraud Investigation. Seventy-Three Per Cent of Visa Holders Are Indian.
news.excerpt: Vice President Vance and the Labor Department's inspector general have fired dozens of subpoenas targeting healthcare fraud, wage kickbacks, and what they call a system 'tied to cartels.' For hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in America, the scrutiny just got personal.

nri-world.nri_angle: Trivedi's appointment extends the growing list of Indian-origin CEOs running American public companies — from P&G to Vanguard to Apple's COO — a pattern rooted in deep technical expertise and long operational tenures that the diaspora's career architecture uniquely produces.

nri-world.title: Five Days, Zero Tickets Required: Lincoln Center's India Week Returns With Garba, Comedy, and the Biggest Silent Disco in South Asian New York

nri-world.nri_angle: India Week is the largest curated celebration of Indian arts and culture at a major American performing arts institution, and every event is free — a deliberate message that Indian culture belongs on the country's biggest cultural stages, not behind a paywall.

nri-world.title: Nita Ambani Proposes an India-America Health Alliance at AAPI's Sold-Out Tampa Convention. The Diaspora's Physicians Are Listening.

nri-world.image_caption: Nita Ambani, Founder and Chairperson of Reliance Foundation
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin physicians are the single largest ethnic bloc in American medicine, and AAPI is their institutional voice. The proposed India-America Health Alliance would channel diaspora medical expertise back into India's healthcare system — turning professional success abroad into public health impact at home.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Thirty-Seven Charged, Twenty-Four Arrested: The US Crackdown on Indian Crime Gangs That Extorted the Diaspora

nri-world.nri_angle: The Bishnoi and Bhagwanpuria gangs directly targeted NRI community leaders and business figures in the US and Canada through extortion, using threats of violence delivered via WhatsApp. A Thousand Oaks, California resident was allegedly threatened with a $5 million demand.

nri-world.title: Seven Jewels, One Community: Inside AIA–New York's 2026 Gala Honouring the Diaspora's Finest
nri-world.excerpt: From a Padma Bhushan oncologist to a Harvard MBA building an AI startup, the oldest Indian American organisation celebrated the professionals who define the community's ambition.

nri-world.nri_angle: AIA-NY, founded in 1967 as the first national association of Asian Indians in America, honoured seven professionals across medicine, law, tech, and business — a snapshot of the Indian American community's evolution from a small immigrant group to a five-million-strong professional powerhouse.

nri-world.nri_angle: Tushar Kumar, 23, from Haryana becomes the youngest Indian-origin mayor in Britain, part of a growing wave of young British-Indian and Indian-American politicians entering civic leadership across the UK and US.

nri-world.title: From OpenAI to Anthropic to Apple: Indian-Origin Engineers Now Run the AI Departments That Run the World

nri-world.nri_angle: New Zealand's Indian community — now 350,000 strong and six per cent of the population — awaits the first visit by an Indian PM in 40 years, navigating between diplomatic warmth and tightening immigration rules.

nri-world.title: India Just Received a Record $145 Billion From Its Diaspora. For the First Time, America Sent the Most.

nri-world.nri_angle: America is now the single largest source of remittances to India, overtaking the Gulf — a data-driven confirmation of the diaspora's shift from blue-collar Gulf workers to white-collar US professionals.

nri-world.title: She Left Kerala at Six. Now Nithya Raman Wants to Run America's Second-Largest City.
